headline: First Regional Review Conference on Implementation of the Forest Rights Act Held in Bengaluru
fullText:
Ministry of Tribal Affairs

First Regional Review Conference on Implementation of the Forest Rights Act Held in Bengaluru

Southern States apprise Ministry of Tribal Affairs of progress in disposal of claims, recognition of Community Forest Rights and Habitat Rights; time-bound roadmaps called for

10 SEP 2026 7:39PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Tribal Affairs (MoTA), Government of India, convened the first Regional Review Conference on implementation of the Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers (Recognition of Forest Rights) Act, 2006 (FRA) at Bengaluru, Karnataka, today, bringing together senior functionaries of the Tribal Welfare, Revenue and Forest Departments of the five Southern States, namely Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, Kerala, Tamil Nadu and Telangana, to review the status of implementation and deliberate upon a coordinated way forward.

Proceedings commenced with a Welcome Address by the Secretary, Scheduled Tribes Welfare Department, Government of Karnataka, who apprised the gathering of the objectives of the Conference and extended a formal welcome to the dignitaries and delegates, followed by a presentation of traditional tribal dance by artistes representing the tribal communities of Karnataka. This was followed by the Keynote Address of the Joint Secretary, MoTA, and the Special Address of the Secretary, MoTA. The Joint Secretary apprised the Conference that, as on 30 June 2026, over 54 lakh Individual Forest Rights (IFR) claims have been received nationally, with approximately 25.42 lakh titles distributed over nearly 238 lakh acres, while over 10 lakh claims remain pending and 19,845 Community Forest Rights (CFR) stand recognised; the Southern States were called upon to accord priority to time-bound disposal of pending claims, recognition of Community Forest Resource Rights and Habitat Rights of Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTGs), and incorporation of recognised rights in land records. In her Special Address, the Secretary, MoTA, underscored that recognition of rights must translate into tenure security, sustainable livelihoods and convergence with development schemes, leading to the empowerment of tribal communities. The Secretary called for greater attention to Community Forest Rights and Community Forest Resource Rights, noting their potential to strengthen Gram Sabha-led forest governance and community-based livelihoods, and referred to the recent joint advisory issued by MoTA and the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change enabling integration of Community Forest Resource Management Plans with Forest Department working and management plans. Underlining that habitat rights of PVTGs embody living systems of culture, livelihood and traditional knowledge, the Secretary called for their recognition to be undertaken with sensitivity and active community participation.

The Director, FRA, MoTA, apprised the Conference of the national scenario of FRA implementation, with particular focus on progress made by the Southern States, covering issues such as pendency of claims, incorporation of Records of Rights, recognition of Habitat Rights, recognition of Community Forest Resource Rights (CFRR), and the support being extended by the Ministry in this regard. The Deputy Secretary, MoTA, thereafter apprised the Conference of the need for digitisation of FRA records and introduced the National-level FRA Portal, currently under development, and urged States to utilise the Portal and integrate their existing FRA records through Application Programming Interface (API).

State-wise Presentations

Officers of the five Southern States thereafter apprised the Conference of the status of FRA implementation in their respective States, as summarised below:

Karnataka: Of 2,95,176 applications received, 16,700 Forest Rights Titles have been distributed and 15,553 claims remain under verification; delay in constitution of Taluk and Zilla Panchayats has affected functioning of the Sub-Divisional and District Level Committees, and re-verification of rejected claims through 'Mahajaru' committees is under progress, with FRA beneficiary data being integrated with the State's FRUITS and Bhoomi platforms for scheme convergence.

Tamil Nadu: 15,838 titles issued in Phase-I stand digitised, while 41,692 fresh claims received under Phase-II are under verification, supported by a State-wide FRA Atlas, dedicated District FRA Cells and structured capacity-building of Forest Rights Committees.

Andhra Pradesh: As on 31 August 2026, 2,27,300 Individual and 1,225 Community titles stand distributed against 2,90,874 claims received, with an integrated land-record and welfare-delivery model linking the Giribhumi FRA portal with the State's revenue and banking systems.

Telangana: 2,30,735 Individual and 102 Community titles have been distributed against 6,55,249 claims received, supported by a fully digitised Online RoFR Title Granting System integrated with the BhuBharathi revenue portal, conferred the SKOCH Award of Excellence (Gold, 2024).

Kerala: 29,545 Individual and 286 Community titles have been recognised, with pendency of 1,616 individual and 108 community claims attributed mainly to survey and verification processes, and six Forest Villages converted into Revenue Villages.

The Ministry called upon the Southern States to ensure time-bound disposal and reconciliation of pending and rejected claims, accelerate recognition of Community Forest Resource Rights and PVTG Habitat Rights, complete incorporation of recognised rights in revenue and forest records, and strengthen convergence with livelihood and welfare schemes, with State-specific roadmaps and timelines which were worked out by the respective States.

headline: BEE Showcases Commercial Electric Cooking Solutions to Accelerate India's Transition from LPG to Electricity
fullText:
Ministry of Power

BEE Showcases Commercial Electric Cooking Solutions to Accelerate India's Transition from LPG to Electricity

Invites stakeholders to register for the Go Electric Commercial Electric Cooking Vendor Directory

10 SEP 2026 7:33PM by PIB Delhi

Bureau of Energy Efficiency (BEE), Ministry of Power, Government of India, organized the “Commercial Induction Cooking Showcase & Chef Challenge” in New Delhi, under the theme “Accelerating India’s Electric Cooking Ambition: From Technology Demonstration to Real-World Adoption.” The event brought together policymakers, public sector enterprises, manufacturers, technology providers, chefs, hoteliers, and commercial kitchen operators on a common platform to advance the adoption of energy-efficient electric cooking in India’s commercial and institutional kitchens.

Shri Pankaj Agarwal, Secretary, Ministry of Power, was the Chief Guest. He inaugurated an exhibition featuring commercial e-cooking appliances and technologies from seven leading manufacturers. Shri Krushna Chandra Panigrahy, Director General, BEE, delivered the keynote address, and Ms. Neha Dhingra, Director, CLASP, delivered the welcome address.

Addressing the gathering, Shri Pankaj Agarwal noted that energy security is the real driver behind India's shift to electric cooking. Due to the ongoing global conflict and rising price of LPG, transitioning to e-cooking is not only a strategic shift but also an operational choice. He stated that the enabling base for this transition already exists, citing schemes such as Pradhan Mantri Sahaj Bijli Har Ghar Yojana (SAUBHAGYA) and PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana, which provide a strong foundation for promoting e-cooking appliances in the residential sector. At the same time, he acknowledged that the barriers to wider adoption have been behavioural and infrastructural, ranging from chef and consumer comfort with the taste of food cooked on induction to gaps in local distribution capacity. Looking ahead, he identified awareness creation as the fastest lever to drive demand and accelerate the mainstreaming of electric cooking across the country.

In his keynote address, Shri Krushna Chandra Panigrahy, Director General, BEE, welcomed representatives from the Ministry of Power, CLASP, industry, hospitality, PSUs, manufacturers, and chefs, and thanked them for their role in advancing India's e-cooking ecosystem. He said India's energy transition isn't just about cleaner energy sources; it is also about using energy more efficiently, and electric cooking brings together efficiency, energy security, convenience, and sustainability in one shift. He announced that BEE is inviting manufacturers, distributors, system integrators, and solution providers to register for the Go Electric Commercial Electric Cooking Vendor Directory, a public platform that will help hotels, restaurants, canteens, hospitals, and institutions find credible providers. He also shared that BEE is working with the Bureau of Indian Standards to develop a Standards & Labeling framework for commercial induction hobs. Shri. Panigrahy informed that BEE’s objective is to move beyond individual demonstration projects towards a mature commercial e-cooking ecosystem, "where users have confidence in the technology, manufacturers understand market requirements, and policymakers have the evidence needed to support its scale-up."

The inaugural session was followed by a Commercial Induction Chef Challenge, where three chefs prepared dishes using induction cooktops. The demonstration enabled participants to observe the cooking performance, ease of use, heat control, and cooking time of induction technology.

The event concluded with closing remarks from BEE, reiterating the Bureau’s commitment to working with the Ministry of Power, CLASP, manufacturers, industry associations, public sector enterprises and commercial kitchen operators to accelerate the adoption of energy-efficient electric cooking across India.

The event reaffirmed the shared responsibility of the Government, industry and hospitality sector to move India’s commercial kitchens from technology demonstration to real-world adoption, in line with the vision of a Viksit and Atmanirbhar Bharat.

The Government of India set up the Bureau of Energy Efficiency (BEE) on1st March, 2002 under the provisions of the Energy Conservation Act, 2001. The mission of the Bureau of Energy Efficiency is to assist in developing policies and strategies with a thrust on self-regulation and market principles.

A key objective is reducing the energy intensity of the Indian economy. BEE coordinates with designated consumers, designated agencies and other organizations. It recognises, identifies and utilises the existing resources and infrastructure, in performing the functions assigned to it under the Act. The Act also provides for regulatory and promotional functions.

headline: TRAI releases The Standards of Quality of Service (Duration of Advertisements in Television Channels) (Repealing) Regulations, 2026
fullText:
Ministry of Communications

TRAI releases The Standards of Quality of Service (Duration of Advertisements in Television Channels) (Repealing) Regulations, 2026

10 SEP 2026 7:24PM by PIB Delhi

Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) issued The Standards of Quality of Service (Duration of Advertisements in Television Channels) (Repealing) Regulations, 2026 (4 of 2026) dated 10.09.2026 to repeal the Standards of Quality of Service (Duration of Advertisements in Television Channels) Regulations, 2012 (15 of 2012) dated 14th May 2012, along with all orders and directions issued thereunder, with effect from the date of its notification in the Official Gazette.

The Standards of Quality of Service (Duration of Advertisements in Television Channels) Regulations, 2012 prescribes a ceiling of twelve minutes of advertisements in a clock hour in broadcast of a programme. The regulations empower the Authority to issue order or direction to service providers to protect the interests of the subscribers or for ensuring compliance of the regulations.

These Regulations were primarily intended to monitor and enforce, as a quality-of-service measure, the advertisement duration ceiling prescribed under rule 7, sub-rule (11) of the Cable Television Networks Rules, 1994.

The Ministry of Information and Broadcasting (MIB), vide notification published in the Official Gazette on 21st August 2026, omitted sub-rule (11) of rule 7 of the Cable Television Networks Rules, 1994, thereby removing the twelve-minute advertisement duration cap prescribed for television channels. The removal of the cap has been undertaken in view of the significant changes in the television broadcasting sector, increased competition and consumer choice, and with a view to enable fair competition and ensuring ease of doing business in the television broadcasting sector.

In view of the removal of the advertisement duration ceiling by the Central Government, continuation of the corresponding regulatory provisions under the TRAI Regulations would be inconsistent with the Rule 7(11) of the Cable Television Networks Rules, 1994.

headline: Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal Calls for Accelerating India-Russia Economic Partnership to Achieve $100 Billion Bilateral Trade by 2030
fullText:
Ministry of Commerce & Industry

Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal Calls for Accelerating India-Russia Economic Partnership to Achieve $100 Billion Bilateral Trade by 2030

Shri Piyush Goyal Highlights Opportunities to Expand India’s Exports to Russia Across Pharmaceuticals, Auto Components and Food Products

Shri Goyal Invites Russian Businesses to Utilize India’s Plug-and-Play Industrial Corridors to Manufacture in India

10 SEP 2026 7:10PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal today called for an accelerated India-Russia economic and industrial partnership, urging businesses from both countries to work towards achieving the target of $100 billion in bilateral trade and $50 billion in two-way investment by 2030. Addressing the INNOPROM India 2026 Co-Chair Plenary Session with Russian Minister of Industry and Trade Mr. Anton Alikhanov in New Delhi, Shri Goyal said that the targets set by the two Heads of State would be a measure of the performance of both governments and businesses.

Shri Goyal said that increasing bilateral trade from the current base of around $60 billion to $100 billion would require adding about $40 billion in the next four years and sustained double-digit growth year-on-year. He stressed that achieving this would require significant efforts not only from the governments but equally from businesses in both countries.

Highlighting the opportunities for diversifying bilateral trade, Shri Goyal said that Indian exports of meat and edible meat products had more than doubled from $36 million to $97 million, an increase of nearly 170 per cent. Fish and aquatic products grew from $123 million to $159 million, an increase of nearly 30 per cent, while exports of edible vegetables rose from $38 million to $54 million, an increase of 40 per cent. Exports of coffee, tea and spices increased by 13 per cent to $116 million, while products of the milling industry had nearly doubled.

Shri Goyal said these figures reflected growing demand in the Russian market for products from Indian farmers, food processors, micro, small and medium enterprises and MSME exporters. He noted that only a small portion of the potential had been tapped so far. Referring to the complementarity between the two economies, he said there were several products where Russia is a significant importer and India is a significant exporter globally, but India is not yet a significant exporter to Russia. He identified pharmaceuticals, auto components, tractors and food products among the opportunities waiting to be explored.

The Minister said that non-energy trade between the two countries remained much smaller than its potential and represented the headroom that needed to be filled to move bilateral trade from $60 billion to $100 billion. He said rebalancing bilateral trade through greater Indian exports of pharmaceuticals, engineering goods, chemicals, textiles, food products, marine products and auto products would be central to achieving the target.

On investment, Shri Goyal said that the India-Russia priority investment projects mechanism is currently tracking 40 live investment projects across advanced manufacturing, energy, mining, railways and emerging technologies. He called upon the Russian side to help open the doors wider for Indian investments in Russia in pharmaceuticals, IT, artificial intelligence, services, engineering and railways, so that the $50 billion investment target becomes genuinely a two-way street.

Shri Goyal said India and Russia are fast-tracking a new bilateral investment treaty to provide investors on both sides with the legal certainty they seek while finalising investment destinations. He also said that India and the Eurasian Economic Union, comprising Russia, Belarus, Kazakhstan, Armenia and the Kyrgyz Republic, had launched formal free trade negotiations last year and that India was committed to concluding them early, opening new markets for industries and, importantly, MSMEs.

The Minister said that the two countries continue to strengthen national and local currency settlement mechanisms, noting that payment friction, more often than tariffs, slows trade on the ground. He also highlighted investments in the physical backbone of the bilateral relationship, including the International North-South Transport Corridor and the Chennai-Vladivostok maritime corridor, stressing that connectivity is a part of trade policy and not merely infrastructure.

Shri Goyal outlined five specific asks for businesses and officials of both countries. First, he urged businesses to finalise at least one deal before leaving Delhi, identify one new friend and partner, and take forward at least one concrete project. Second, he called upon businesses to add a new non-energy line to their trade and investment plans, particularly in pharmaceuticals, engineering goods, chemicals, auto components, tractor parts, textiles, food, agri-tech and marine products, stating that these sectors would help achieve the $100 billion bilateral trade target.

Third, Shri Goyal called upon Russian industry to manufacture in India and not only sell in the country. He said India's national industrial corridors are investment-ready, with plug-and-play infrastructure available for global partners. He highlighted India's youthful talent and skilled labour as an important resource for Russian companies, noting that such skilled labour may be difficult to find in Russia.

Fourth, he urged Indian industry to go to Russia not merely as visitors but as investors and exporters, and to cultivate friendships, new partnerships and new business potential.

Fifth, Shri Goyal called upon officials on both sides to listen to industry and identify the factors that are blocking trade and investment. He asked them to examine whether payment systems, certification requirements, standards, logistics, visa access or approvals were creating difficulties. He assured the Russian side that he and his colleagues stood ready to help make the entire journey seamless, smooth and exciting.

Highlighting India's strengths as an investment and manufacturing destination, Shri Goyal said India offers scale and a rapidly expanding industrial manufacturing base under initiatives including Make in India, Digital India, the industrial park scheme and Startup India. He said India invests $130 billion every year in creating new infrastructure and strengthening its capacity in airports, ports, expressways, railways, inland waterways, power infrastructure, water infrastructure and industrial parks. He said there is a strong drive to create the right ecosystem and infrastructure to host global partners in India.

Shri Goyal said India provides talent and skills in abundance, along with a young and aspirational population willing to innovate, design and co-design, co-create and co-manufacture with its global partners. He said Russia brings decades of engineering excellence, particularly in aerospace, metallurgy, nuclear technology and mining. He emphasised that when the strengths of India and Russia come together, the relationship can go beyond trade and build resilience into both economies.

Referring to the longstanding India-Russia relationship, Shri Goyal said it had weathered seven decades of a changing world. He said the task before the two countries now was not merely continuity but acceleration. Quoting Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, he said, “The greatest strength of India-Russia relations lies in trust. This trust provides both direction and momentum to our joint efforts and serves as the launchpad inspiring new dreams and aspirations.”

Shri Goyal said the presence of INNOPROM in India for the first time in its history was significant. He noted that for over a decade, INNOPROM, the Global Industrial Technology Exhibition, had served as a platform where Russian engineering and manufacturing presented themselves to the world. He said bringing the platform to India demonstrated where the two nations now stand and reflected their readiness to move “from protocols to production, from intent to industry.”

Shri Goyal said the two ministries had been working closely over the past several months to deepen economic and industrial cooperation and expressed confidence that the visit of Russian Minister of Industry and Trade Mr. Anton Alikhanov would accelerate this progress.

Concluding his address, Shri Goyal thanked Minister Alikhanov and the entire Russian delegation for their partnership and wished INNOPROM India 2026 and all businesses represented at the exhibition a productive final stretch.

headline: India Charts Course to Become Global Hub for Ship Ownership, Leasing and Maritime Finance: Sarbananda Sonowal
fullText:
Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways

India Charts Course to Become Global Hub for Ship Ownership, Leasing and Maritime Finance: Sarbananda Sonowal

GIFT City Emerges as the Enabling Platform for India's Maritime Finance Ambitions

Sonowal Addressed the India Ship Leasing and Financing Summit at the IFSC in GIFT City

10 SEP 2026 6:48PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister of Ports, Shipping & Waterways, Sarbananda Sonowal, was the Chief Guest at the India Ship Leasing and Financing Summit, organised by the International Financial Services Centres Authority (IFSCA) in collaboration with the Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways (MoPSW), at the GIFT City Club, Gandhinagar, today.

The summit brought together policymakers, ship owners, lessors, charterers, financiers and maritime stakeholders to deliberate on India's push to build a comprehensive ship ownership, leasing and financing ecosystem, with GIFT City positioned as the platform enabling this ambition.

Addressing the gathering, Sonowal invoked India's maritime legacy, tracing it to the Indus Valley Civilization and the ancient port of Lothal in Gujarat. "This gathering marks a significant milestone in our collective journey to position India, and particularly GIFT City, as a global maritime hub for a comprehensive maritime value chain ecosystem, encompassing ship leasing, owning, financing, insurance, brokering and other ancillary services," Sonowal said.

The Minister pointed to India's growing fleet footprint, with 38 ship lessors now registered and collectively leasing 43 vessels, taking total leasing capacity past 2.99 million DWT, of which 24 vessels now fly the Indian flag. He added that 41 domestic and international banks have set up in the IFSC, extending close to USD 60.1 million in funding to ship leasing entities, with DGMA's first regional office opening in GIFT City set to further strengthen this ecosystem for shipowners and operators.

Sonowal outlined key reforms enabling Indian shipping to compete globally, including exemption from licensing requirements under the Coastal Shipping Act, 2025, for foreign vessels on charter, and permission for GIFT IFSC-based shipping companies to own foreign-flag vessels. On the latter, Sonowal said, "More fundamentally, it marks a shift in how we count our fleet, from tonnage that flies our flag to tonnage that we own and control. PM Narendra Modi ji's dynamic leadership has carried GIFT City from thought to fruition, and it is now poised to be the launchpad for India's next wave of maritime growth”

The Union Minister further cited Modi government's financial commitments to the sector, including the ₹25,000 crore Maritime Development Fund expected to catalyse investments of up to ₹1.5 lakh crore by 2030, and the Shipbuilding Financial Assistance Scheme (SBFAS) 2.0, with a revised outlay of ₹24,736 crore extended to 2036, both aimed at strengthening Indian shipyards and vessel ownership.

The Union Minister attributed this momentum to the vision of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, referencing the Maritime India Vision (MIV) 2030 and Maritime Amrit Kaal Vision (MAKV) 2047 as roadmaps to expand India's fleet, boost port capacity and coastal shipping, and place India among the top five global shipbuilding nations. He also cited India's emergence as the world's largest ship recycling nation, its share of global tonnage rising from 30.1% in 2024 to 35.4% in 2025.

Vijay Kumar, Secretary, MoPSW; K. Rajaraman, Chairperson, IFSCA; and Hareet Shukla, Principal Secretary, Ports & Transport, Government of Gujarat, were also present.

headline: Over 1.44 crore Scheduled Caste students supported with scholarships amounting to Rs 12,773 crore
fullText:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment

Over 1.44 crore Scheduled Caste students supported with scholarships amounting to Rs 12,773 crore

Key reforms introduced under SHRESHTA, National Overseas Scholarship and National Fellowship Schemes to ensure timely admissions, transparency and accountability

More than 1.01 Crore OBC and EBC students receive scholarship assistance of Rs 2,445.05 Crore

10 SEP 2026 6:16PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Social Justice and Empowerment, Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, Government of India, has undertaken transformative reforms and significantly expanded the reach of its scholarship and educational support schemes. These initiatives are aimed at strengthening access to education for students from Scheduled Castes (SCs), Other Backward Classes (OBCs) and Economically Backward Classes (EBCs), while making programme implementation more timely, transparent and accountable.

More than 1.44 crore SC students have benefited under the Pre-Matric and Post-Matric Scholarship Schemes. The Scholarships amounting to Rs 12,773 crore have been disbursed to support their educational advancement and help them pursue learning opportunities without financial barriers.

Similarly, more than 1.01 crore students belonging to OBC and EBC communities have received support under the Pre-Matric and Post-Matric Scholarship Schemes, with assistance amounting to Rs 2,445.05 crore. This extensive outreach reflects the Government’s commitment to promoting inclusive education and equal opportunities for students from disadvantaged backgrounds.

Under the Scheme for Residential Education for Students in High Schools in Targeted Areas (SHRESHTA), the annual National Entrance Test for SHRESHTA (NETS) examination schedule has been advanced from May to December. The reform is aimed at facilitating timely counselling and admissions, ensuring alignment with the academic calendar, and minimising delays and student drop-outs.

The revised schedule will enable eligible students to complete the admission process within the prescribed academic cycle and begin their studies without avoidable disruption.

To strengthen the authenticity of documents and prevent fraudulent claims, a system for on-the-spot verification of income and caste certificates directly from the issuing authorities was introduced under the National Overseas Scholarship Scheme from the academic year 2024–25.

The measure reinforces the integrity of the selection process and helps ensure that scholarship benefits reach genuine and eligible candidates aspiring to pursue higher education abroad.

Under the National Fellowship for SC Students Scheme, a mandatory seven-day grievance-submission window was introduced from the academic year 2025–26 following the declaration of the UGC-NET and Joint CSIR-UGC NET results.

The stipulated window enables students to report discrepancies within a defined timeframe. It also promotes timely resolution of grievances, strengthens accountability and enhances transparency and trust in the fellowship-selection process.

Through expanded financial assistance and process-driven reforms, the Ministry continues to build a more inclusive, efficient and student-centric educational support ecosystem. These measures reaffirm the Government’s commitment to empowering disadvantaged communities through equitable access to quality education and opportunities for academic advancement.

- Under SHRESHTA, the National Entrance Test for SHRESHTA (NETS) schedule has been advanced from May to December.
- The SHRESHTA reform aims to support timely counselling and admissions, align the process with the academic calendar, reduce delays and minimise student drop-outs.
- From the academic year 2024–25, the National Overseas Scholarship Scheme introduced on-the-spot verification of income and caste certificates directly from issuing authorities.
- This verification measure is intended to prevent fraudulent claims and ensure benefits reach eligible candidates pursuing higher education abroad.
- From the academic year 2025–26, the National Fellowship for SC Students Scheme introduced a mandatory seven-day grievance-submission window after the declaration of UGC-NET and Joint CSIR-UGC NET results.

headline: From Need to Opportunity: DEPwD, ALIMCO and EkStep Join Hands to Build a Digital Bridge for Persons with Disabilities
fullText:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment

From Need to Opportunity: DEPwD, ALIMCO and EkStep Join Hands to Build a Digital Bridge for Persons with Disabilities

10 SEP 2026 6:12PM by PIB Delhi

A new digital architecture is set to bring Persons with Disabilities (PwDs) and the opportunities, services and support they need closer than ever. The Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities (DEPwD), Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment, Artificial Limbs Manufacturing Corporation of India (ALIMCO) and EkStep Foundation, Bengaluru, today signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) in New Delhi to establish an institutional framework for the design, development, implementation and scaling of the Purple Dots – UBI (Unified Benefits Interface) Initiative.

Conceptualised by DEPwD, the Purple Dots Initiative seeks to address a fundamental challenge in disability inclusion—not merely the availability of benefits and services, but the ability of a person to discover the right opportunity, service or support at the right time and place. At its core, a “Purple Dot” is a simple digital profile through which a Person with Disability can indicate who they are and what they need—whether it is employment, assistive technology such as a wheelchair, skill development, training or any other support. Similarly, employers, service providers, NGOs, philanthropic organisations and other institutions can create their own “dots” to indicate the opportunities, services and resources they offer.

By bringing these dots together through an open and interoperable digital infrastructure, the initiative seeks to create a connected ecosystem in which needs and opportunities can discover each other locally and efficiently. An open digital protocol will enable ecosystem stakeholders to interact and respond to identified needs in real time, helping move disability inclusion from fragmented access towards seamless discovery, linkage and participation.

The MoU establishes a collaborative framework for taking the Purple Dots – UBI (Unified Benefits Interface) Initiative from concept to implementation and scale. It envisages enabling Persons with Disabilities to discover and connect with relevant government entitlements, services, employment opportunities, training programmes, assistive devices and support systems offered by Government Departments, private-sector entities, civil society organisations, NGOs, philanthropic institutions and other ecosystem partners.

The initiative represents a significant step towards strengthening accessibility and inclusion through digital public infrastructure. Rather than creating isolated systems for individual schemes or institutions, Purple Dots seeks to enable different actors in the disability ecosystem to connect and collaborate through an interoperable framework, thereby improving the visibility and reach of services and opportunities that are already available.

EkStep Foundation, a philanthropy instrumental in conceiving and architecting Digital Public Infrastructure/ Digital Public Good initiatives for large-scale societal transformation, is partnering with DEPwD and ALIMCO to bring its experience of building open and collaborative digital ecosystems to the disability sector. The partnership seeks to strengthen the ability of local ecosystem players to discover one another and connect Persons with Disabilities with relevant services, opportunities and support, building on capabilities that already exist across the country.

The collaboration brings together the mandate and nationwide reach of DEPwD, the experience and capabilities of ALIMCO in the disability sector, and EkStep Foundation’s experience in enabling ecosystem-led digital innovation at scale. Together, the partners seek to make support and services more accessible, discoverable and connected for Persons with Disabilities across districts, while strengthening the participation of Government, industry, civil society and other stakeholders in creating an inclusive ecosystem.

The MoU-signing ceremony was attended by Ms. Manmeet Kaur Nanda, Additional Secretary; Shri Ashish Thakre, Director; Shri Pradeep A., Director; and Shri Sandeep Kumar, Under Secretary, from DEPwD. From ALIMCO, Shri Pankaj Dwivedi, Assistant Manager; and Ms. Priya Grover, Assistant Manager, were present. Shri Ikpreet Singh, Director; Shri Gaurav Gupta represented EkStep Foundation, Bengaluru.

The Purple Dots Initiative envisages a future in which a person’s need does not remain invisible and an available opportunity does not remain undiscovered—where digital connectivity becomes a practical bridge between Persons with Disabilities and the ecosystem of services, opportunities and support around them.

This version deliberately uses “Need to make Opportunity visible and localize” as the news hook, making the Purple Dots concept understandable to a general newspaper reader rather than presenting the MoU merely as an institutional agreement.

headline: Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah chairs the third meeting of the Governing Body of the NIDM in New Delhi
fullText:
Ministry of Home Affairs

Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah chairs the third meeting of the Governing Body of the NIDM in New Delhi

Under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, over the past 12 years, there has been a fundamental transformation in both the approach and the methodology of disaster management

Earlier, disasters were viewed only from the perspective of relief and rehabilitation, today we are advancing into a new era of risk reduction, early warning systems, and Zero Casualty

We have successfully tackled many disasters with Zero Casualty, which is a major achievement

The goal of Modi govt. is to make disaster-resilient villages and disaster-resilient cities, we must move forward by keeping this as a priority

Today, NIDM has become a national centre for research, innovation, and capacity building, new horizons will have to be explored by integrating universities into it

Due to environmental protection, risk reduction, resilience, and a comprehensive national vision, India is gradually emerging as an ideal model in the world

Moving beyond training and guidelines, we should also advance towards a ‘Whole of Government’ approach in building a system to stand firmly against disasters

In the era of global warming, climate change, and new scientific innovations, the relevance and need for both NIDM and NDMA will grow even further in days to come

Mobile application developed for disaster management should be widely promoted and adopted across the higher, secondary, and primary education sectors

Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi has also taken the decision to ensure that the distribution of disaster relief funds is undertaken through a scientific and systematic process

Just as we adopted a ‘Whole of Government’ approach to effectively address disasters, we must move forward with the same approach to further strengthen and institutionalise disaster management

Under the Modi Government, the allocation to SDRF has increased nearly fourfold, while allocation to NDRF has increased nearly threefold

Along with transforming the approach to disaster management, Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi has also laid special emphasis on environmental protection

At one point, NIDM was confined to a corner of Krishi Bhavan, former PM Atal Ji brought it under MHA and gave it a new lease of life, PM Modi further revitalised the institution by facilitating the allocation of land for it, today the transformed and expanded NIDM stands before the nation as a testament to this vision and commitment

All stakeholders should establish a dedicated and focused cell within their respective departments to ensure the effective implementation of these agenda items, the heads of the respective departments should review the progress once every three months and accord the necessary priority to their implementation

10 SEP 2026 6:09PM by PIB Delhi

Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah today chaired the third meeting of the Governing Body of the National Institute of Disaster Management (NIDM) in New Delhi. The meeting was attended by the Union Home Secretary, Vice-Chancellor of Delhi University, Member and Head of Department of the National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA), Director General of the National Disaster Response Force (NDRF), Secretary of the Department of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, Director General of the India Meteorological Department (IMD), Director of the Lal Bahadur Shastri National Academy of Administration (LBSNAA), Executive Director of NIDM, and senior officials from several Central Ministries and State Governments.

Addressing the meeting, the Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation said that under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi there has been a comprehensive transformation in both the approach and methodology of disaster management over the last 12 years. The Modi Government has completely transformed the entire disaster management system, set the goal of ‘Zero Casualty’ and taken the country towards achieving this objective. We have also successfully faced several disasters with ‘Zero Casualty’, which is a major achievement. Shri Shah said that earlier disasters were viewed only from the perspective of relief and rehabilitation. Today, we have entered a new era based on three pillars - risk reduction, early warning systems and ‘Zero Casualty’. This is a matter of pride for all of us. He said that in this direction, the ‘Whole of Government’ approach is increasingly becoming an integral part of our work culture. Whenever a disaster occurs, all government departments actively respond. Now, with the strength of new research, we should take this process forward with greater speed and ensure continuous monitoring. Just as a ‘Whole of Government’ approach has been adopted in dealing with disasters, we must also move forward with a ‘Whole of Government’ approach to further strengthen the disaster management system.

Union Home Minister said that along with the transformation in the approach to disaster management, Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi has also laid special emphasis on environmental protection. He said that ultimately environmental protection is the most effective means of preventing disasters. Environmental protection, risk reduction, resilience and a broad national vision are enabling India to gradually emerge as a model for the world. Initiatives such as Mission LiFE (Lifestyle for Environment), Pro-Planet People and the International Solar Alliance (ISA) are making an important contribution to disaster prevention. Shri Shah said that the ‘Zero Casualty’ approach should not be applied only at the site of a disaster. Zero Casualty can also be achieved by preventing disasters from occurring in the first place. Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi has envisioned a safe and balanced world, going beyond the conventional approach of world leaders.

Shri Amit Shah said that there was a time when the predecessor of NIDM, the National Centre for Disaster Management was lying almost inactive in a corner of Krishi Bhawan. However, in 2003, the then Prime Minister Shri Atal Bihari Vajpayee took the historic decision to give it a new lease of life. Keeping in view the wide scope of the subject and the need for coordination among various agencies, it was decided to bring the institution under the Ministry of Home Affairs. Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi has played a significant role in revitalizing the institution. NIDM has emerged in its present form with a transformed and strengthened role before the country.

Union Home Minister said that the relevance and significance of both NIDM and NDMA are going to increase further in the coming days. The number of disasters is likely to increase due to global warming and climate change. At the same time, new types of disasters may also emerge due to new applications of science and their expanding areas of use. Keeping all these aspects in mind, the two institutions share responsibilities ranging from policy-making to training and implementation. In some areas, both institutions are also working together.

Shri Amit Shah directed all stakeholders to constitute a dedicated cell in their respective departments for implementation of the agenda. He said that departmental heads should conduct a review meeting of the cell at least once every three months and accord priority to this subject.

Union Home Minister Shri Amit Shah said that NDMA and NIDM should study research being undertaken across the world in the field of disaster management and make efforts to implement its findings in India in accordance with local requirements. The Department of Agriculture should focus on permanent preparedness to deal with locust swarm attacks originating from the Pakistan side. He said that the best practices being adopted in other countries to deal with such attacks should be implemented in India. Shri Shah added that seriousness should be ensured in disaster management training and priority should be given to those who are genuinely committed to the subject in disaster management training programmes.

Union Home Minister said that NIDM and NDMA should jointly issue guidelines for the entire country. These guidelines should clearly specify what should and should not be done in the event of each type of disaster and how it should be done. NIDM should undertake the training component while the NDRF, State Disaster Response Forces (SDRFs) and other concerned agencies should work together to implement these guidelines on the ground.

Shri Amit Shah said that it is extremely important to prepare a document, through research, identifying the causes of disasters. Effective prevention and rescue measures can be developed on this basis. After every disaster, a joint team of NDMA and NIDM should be constituted, including the NDRF and SDRF. These four institutions should jointly study the causes of the damage and prepare a detailed report.

Shri Amit Shah said that NIDM has emerged as a national centre for research, innovation, policy support, training and departmental cooperation. We need to further strengthen these four pillars and explore new horizons. There are still unexplored areas in research, innovation, training, policy support and departmental cooperation that we should seek to address in the coming days. He said that NIDM has already taken steps in this direction. There is a need to take knowledge and best practices beyond departmental silos. In the coming days we must develop the habit of working in a coordinated manner, rising above departmental boundaries.

Union Home Minister said that Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi has decided that the distribution of disaster funds should also be carried out through a scientific process. The allocation under the State Disaster Response Fund (SDRF) has increased nearly fourfold, while the allocation under the National Disaster Response Fund (NDRF) has increased nearly threefold. Around ₹2.5 lakh crore has been spent in this sector over the last 11 years, which is a major achievement. The Disaster Management Act was amended after 20 years. The concept of Urban Disaster Management Authorities was introduced and such authorities have also been established. The process of creating digital disaster databases at the national and state levels has begun. The National Crisis Management Committee (NCMC) has been accorded statutory status. In addition, the 16th Finance Commission has provided for ₹2 lakh crore for this period.

Shri Amit Shah said that the mobile application that has been developed needs to be widely promoted through primary, secondary and higher education. The Government is making every possible effort to strengthen NIDM. Recently, four acres of land have also been allocated for the institution. NIDM is working towards developing itself as a world-class model institution, and both its campuses are functioning smoothly. Shri Shah said that while enhancing international cooperation is undoubtedly commendable, our priority must continue to focus on the five lakh villages of the country. Keeping this priority in mind, there should be no objection to learning as much as possible from the world and enabling the world to learn as much as possible from us. He stated that the Modi government's goal is to create disaster-resilient villages and cities, and we must move forward by prioritizing this objective.

Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah said that a provision should be made for at least one top-level meeting of NIDM to be held every year so that the meetings are meaningful and outcome-oriented and effective implementation of the decisions taken is ensured. He said that through this institution, we must transform knowledge into capacity, capacity into preparedness and preparedness into outcomes, so that together we can achieve the goal of ‘Zero Casualty’.
